_doc: The address book for dated lake-shore states. Terrain epochs select a shoreline by id; they never silently reuse another epoch's line. A `planned` state has geometry null until its owning ticket supplies a trace; a `supplied` state has its own trace and no ground to stand it on yet; an `active` state has both. An observation from OUTSIDE a state's own terrain epoch may bound it, but it may not become its adopted line — an observation from inside that epoch may, because an epoch is by definition one state of the ground, and the state must then say how far the reading's date stands from its address date and what that costs. Where independent readings differ, disagreement_bands points to the full spread rather than an average.

states.label: 15 August 1812 — natural river mouth and pre-harbor shore
states.note: SUPPLIED by T-1243 (piece 1 of T-0468). It is still deliberately not an alias of shore_1835_harbor_cut: the two lines come from different sheets at different dates, and the cut, the piers and the harbour reach that define the 1835 state are all absent here. `status` is `supplied` and not `active` because the line exists and the GROUND does not — epoch e1830_natural has no terrain_spec, no heightfield and no meshes, and T-1244 to T-1246 own them. An 1812 scene cannot render this state until they land.

evidence_limit.adopted_reading_is_eighteen_years_late: The address date is 15 August 1812 and the only plan of the natural mouth this project holds is Harrison's of 24 February 1830. The two dates sit inside ONE ground state — epoch e1830_natural runs 1780-01-01 to 1833-06-30, and the condition that defines it, a baymouth bar closing the river and deflecting it south, is stated inside the bracket at both ends: by Swearingen standing on the ground in August 1803 ('dead water, owing to its being stopped up at the mouth, by the washing of sand, from the lakes') and by Harrison drawing it in 1830. What is NOT carried by that is the bar's exact planform: a sand bar migrates, and nothing here claims the 1812 line stood where the 1830 line stands. The line is graded inferred for that reason as well as for the re-engraving.
evidence_limit.the_outlet_itself_is_off_this_sheet: Harrison's neat lines stop at about local N -177, and the mouth is not inside them: the sheet letters 'Old Mouth of River very shallow' beside the channel at about local E +1221, N -78 and the channel runs on south past the frame. Swearingen puts the fort site 'a half mile above the mouth', which from the committed palisade at local N +221 would place the outlet near N -584 — close to the Madison Street line the e1834_harbor_cut spec names as the natural outlet. This state adopts NO outlet position: the reach between the foot of this sheet and the mouth is unread, and the half mile bounds it rather than fixing it.
evidence_limit.what_is_not_here: No lake edge, no water polygon, no sand bar and no hydrology. The bar is drawn on this sheet and lettered 'Sand' and 'Gravel', but it is not enclosed by the traced water body and is not published as an island; it belongs with the water traces.
evidence_limit.excluded_by_date: The channel Harrison letters 'cut by the Soldiers in 1828' is sixteen years later than this state's address date and is cut out of the trace. About 60 m of its western entrance survives inside south_shore_pre_cut and is named in that file's known_defects.

states.label: 1 July 1835 — harbor cut and eroding south shore
states.note: Wright's 1834 line is the scene's primary reading where it exists. Rees & Rucker's 1849 line is fourteen years late and is only a lower bound below Twelfth Street: the 1835 water's edge stood on it or east of it. The two fitted sheets overlap from local N -1300 to -2000 and differ at every 100 m station. Their full spread is the named band; no midpoint or smoothed compromise is adopted.

states.label: 1880s — Illinois Central edge and post-fire fill
states.note: Reserved for T-0473. It is deliberately not an alias of either earlier state: the 1880s lake edge must represent the Illinois Central corridor and period fill rather than the natural or 1835 shore. T-0473 owns the representative scene date and the sourced trace.
